name: Karur Vysya Bank Ltd
title: Karur Vysya Bank Ltd - 590003 - Transcript of the Conference Call

read.thesis: KVB delivered record FY26 profit of INR2,500 crore (ROA 1.93%) but guided FY27 NIM to 3.75–3.8% and ROA to 1.7–1.8% as it concedes pricing to protect relationships; credit growth set at industry +1–2%.

utilisation.quote: we started seeing the lower level of utilization in the working capital. 2% to 3%, it is down across the sectors

triggers.label: FY27 NIM guided to 3.75–3.8%
triggers.quote: we expect that NIMs to be in the range of 3.75% to 3.8% for the full year, though we are at 4% plus at the exit quarter of this year
triggers.highlight: NIMs to be in the range of 3.75% to 3.8%

triggers.label: FY27 ROA cut to 1.7–1.8%
triggers.quote: we expect the ROA for the full year to be between 1.7% to 1.8%
triggers.highlight: ROA for the full year to be between 1.7% to 1.8%

triggers.label: Yield concession to retain accounts
triggers.quote: we may have to concede and reduce the rates to existing customers and also for the acquisition also
triggers.highlight: we may have to concede and reduce the rates

triggers.label: Working-capital utilisation down 2–3%
triggers.quote: we started seeing the lower level of utilization in the working capital. 2% to 3%, it is down across the sectors
triggers.highlight: lower level of utilization in the working capital

triggers.label: Competitors pricing aggressively
triggers.quote: The competition is coming from many corners, including a few private banks as well as public sector banks
triggers.highlight: The competition is coming from many corners

triggers.label: Prudential provision INR163 crore for sectors
triggers.quote: We have provided prudentially INR163 crores, I repeat INR163 crores is a onetime towards sectors identified that may get affected due to ongoing geopolitical tensions

guidance.quote: we expect that NIMs to be in the range of 3.75% to 3.8% for the full year
we expect the ROA for the full year to be between 1.7% to 1.8%
We expect our credit growth to be 1% or 2% over the industry growth
Credit cost, I can think around less than 1% we can think of.
GNPA is expected to be less than 1.5% and net NPA to be less than 1% for the full year.
Our cost -to-income ratio would be below 50% as we have been continuously planning
LCR would be maintained around 115% to 120%.
we are planning to open 50 branches

prior_guidance_check.quote: we were able to maintain a NIM for the full year at 3.97%
We have achieved an ROA of 2.1% in this quarter and 1.93% for the full year.
we have conveyed 2% over the industry. So you would have seen RBI last data at the end of March, 16.1%

red_flags.label: Yield concessions to retain accounts
red_flags.quote: we may have to concede and reduce the rates to existing customers and also for the acquisition also

red_flags.label: Lower write-offs and recovery-driven other income
red_flags.quote: that is why consciously, we have gone for a lower write-off compared to earlier years

red_flags.label: Gold loan 30% of book, LTV concentration
red_flags.quote: we maintain an internal cap of 35%

evasions.quote: let us not talk about the competition. Competition can be from any corner.
that some more time is required. Recently, circular has come.
